name: What's the difference between repairing and replacing a hard-to-open window?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between repairing and replacing a hard-to-open window?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing a hard-to-open window focuses on fixing the specific component causing the issue, such as cleaning tracks, replacing balances, or adjusting hardware. This is often a cost-effective solution if the frame is in good condition and only minor parts are failing. Replacing a window involves removing the entire old unit and installing a new one. Replacement is typically considered when the window is severely damaged, outdated, energy inefficient, or multiple components are failing, making repair impractical or more expensive than a new unit.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair fixes specific components like tracks or balances, suitable for minor issues. Replacement is for severely damaged, outdated, or energy-inefficient windows when repair is impractical.
